summary: The diff adds a new Checkout page with an email field and a Pay button, and refactors App routing. The happy path renders, but submitting with an empty or invalid email throws in the console and gives the user no feedback, and the Pay button can be double-submitted. Mobile layout overflows horizontally.

flowsTested.name: Checkout with empty email
flowsTested.notes: TypeError in console, no inline error

flowsTested.name: Checkout at 375px
flowsTested.notes: Horizontal scroll caused by fixed 420px card width

findings.title: Submitting checkout with an empty email crashes the submit handler
findings.description: handleSubmit calls email.trim() before validating, but email is undefined until the input is touched, so the handler throws and the user sees nothing.
findings.expected: Inline error under the email field: 'Enter your email'

evidence.console:
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')
    at handleSubmit (Checkout.tsx:31:22)

fix.explanation: Initialise the email state to an empty string and validate before trimming; render the error message under the input with aria-describedby.

findings.title: Pay button can be double-submitted, creating two orders
findings.description: The button is not disabled while createOrder() is pending, so a double click sends two POST /api/orders requests.
findings.expected: One request; button disabled with a spinner while pending

fix.explanation: Track an isSubmitting state, disable the button while true, and early-return in handleSubmit if already submitting.

findings.title: Checkout card overflows horizontally on mobile
findings.description: The card has a fixed width of 420px, causing horizontal scroll at 375px.

findings.title: Email input has no accessible label
findings.description: The input relies on placeholder text only; screen readers announce it as 'edit text'.

fix.explanation: Add a visible <label htmlFor="email"> or aria-label="Email".

findings.title: Payment failure state could not be tested
findings.description: There is no way to force the payments API to fail locally. Consider adding a mock flag so the error path can be verified.
